mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the past month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts by more than 10% in the past two months signals a decline in demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST decreases by more than 10% in two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in the past month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures over the past three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained RSAFS growth over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% in the past month, it indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.3% in the past month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP by more than 1% in the past quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook worsen.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when GDPC1 decreases by more than 1% in a quarter.
